claim: A canonical smartd config for fleet storage monitoring is 'DEVICESCAN -a -o on -S on -n standby,q -s (S/../.././02|L/../../6/03) -W 4,45,55 -m root@' providing daily short self-tests at 2 AM, Saturday long tests at 3 AM, temperature trip points (4-degree change, 45 warning, 55 critical), and email alerts, enabled via 'systemctl enable --now smartd'.
stance_target: SMART monitoring as a concrete feature/checklist item for ha-linux-agent's storage-health collector on jupiterOS hosts
quoted_support: DEVICESCAN -a -o on -S on -n standby,q -s (S/../.././02|L/../../6/03) -W 4,45,55 -m root@example.com ... Short test daily at 2 AM, long test Saturdays at 3 AM. Temperature monitoring (4-degree change, 45 warning, 55 critical).

claim: Key HDD SMART warning attributes are Reallocated_Sector_Ct, Current_Pending_Sector, Offline_Uncorrectable, UDMA_CRC_Error_Count and Spin_Retry_Count (any nonzero or growing value); for SSDs, Wear_Leveling_Count and Media_Wearout_Indicator; and for NVMe drives the health log fields percentage used, available spare, media and data integrity errors, and critical warning.
stance_target: Which specific SMART/NVMe attributes a fleet agent's storage-health module should gate alerts on
scope_conditions: smartctl -A / NVMe smart-log output on Linux
quoted_support: For NVMe drives, use the NVMe namespace device path: sudo smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1. Key NVMe health metrics: Percentage Used - How much of the SSD lifetime has been consumed; Available Spare - Remaining spare NAND blocks; Media and Data Integrity Errors - Should be 0; Critical Warning - Active warnings.

claim: SMART overall health via 'smartctl -H' returns PASSED/FAILED, where FAILED means 'back up your data immediately'; NVMe devices are queried via namespace paths (/dev/nvme0n1) rather than /dev/sdX.
stance_target: Minimal health-gate check design for the agent's storage collector
quoted_support: Quick health check: sudo smartctl -H /dev/sda. Output: SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED. If this shows FAILED, back up your data immediately.
